source.title: CoT-ICL Lab: A Petri Dish for Studying Chain-of-Thought Learning from In-Context Demonstrations
source.authors: Vignesh Kothapalli; Hamed Firooz; Maziar Sanjabi

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The title in the body differs slightly from the supplied title.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies synthetic CoT in-context learning and argues that models can infer task-specific causal structure without prefix-matching and copying mechanisms. It tests setup effects on CoT-ICL performance, but does not identify or measure induction heads.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CoT-ICL accuracy transitions across training and setup conditions, plus attention analyses of causal-DAG parent selection. It does not measure induction-head formation, previous-token-head composition, [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying, loss by token index, or a bump in training loss. Rows below capture results about setup-dependent ICL performance (V5) and DAG attention findings that do not fit a claim version. Induction-head characterizations in related work are citations, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study trains transformers on synthetic chain-of-thought ICL tasks and reports task accuracy transitions and DAG-parent attention. It never identifies induction heads or previous-token heads. It measures no repeated-token copying, loss by token index, or induction-head formation timing. Section 6.4.1 only argues verbally that its attention patterns go 'beyond' induction-head prefix matching. The accuracy sweeps measure a related but different construct: synthetic task accuracy, not induction-head formation or ICL persistence. So V5 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that CoT speeds accuracy transitions, depth matters at limited K, and more examples let shallow models catch up. Limiting token-processor diversity improves causal-structure learning. The 'beyond induction heads' point is a brief interpretive remark in Section 6.4.1, not a tested result.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains decoder-only transformers on synthetic multi-input CoT-ICL tasks and measures accuracy and DAG-parent attention. It does not reproduce the original induction-head identification or training-dynamics method.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy outcomes vary with vocabulary size, number of in-context examples, chain length, number of parent tokens, token-processor diversity, model depth, and pre-training. Attention-map patterns also differ with token-processor diversity; the paper reports that the DAG patterns were not found in the infinite-token-processor case.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic CoT-ICL tasks, accuracy transitions depend on CoT, depth, vocabulary size, number of examples K, and pre-training. Pre-trained Llama-3.2-1B transitions earlier than a randomly initialised copy. Non-CoT final accuracy is 0.25 vs 0.08.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training setup and model depth shape when transformers acquire synthetic multi-input ICL task accuracy, and CoT accelerates it.

fits_no_version.finding: With fixed token processors, the last-layer attention, averaged over heads, concentrates on the DAG parent tokens. Parent precision rises with accuracy. The pattern is not found with unbounded token processors, where attention relies on previous answer tokens.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformers can learn attention to causal parent tokens in synthetic ICL without prefix-matching, when function diversity is limited.

record.problems: The study's synthetic tokens are not grounded in real-world concepts, as the authors note. It does not directly identify or intervene on induction heads, and its attention-map analysis averages across heads. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the relevant results.
record.rows_left_out: Other synthetic-task accuracy sweeps and token-distribution analyses are not included because they do not add a direct result about induction behaviour or the setup-dependent ICL outcomes represented here. Figures 5–8 and 17–25 contain additional setup sweeps; only the transitions and condition comparisons described in the main text relevant to V5 are recorded.

untested.parts: No induction or previous-token heads identified; no composition or [A][B]…[A]→[B] copying tested.
No induction-head timing, loss bump, or token-index ICL gain measured; only synthetic task-accuracy transitions.
No per-token loss, and no share of ICL attributed to induction heads.
No survey of induction heads across models.
Setup affects synthetic task accuracy, but induction-head formation and ICL persistence are not measured.
Argued in text only; no measurement separates induction heads from other mechanisms in few-shot learning.

record.verdict_notes: The study mentions induction heads only to contrast its DAG-attention analysis with prefix matching. That analysis also averages attention over heads. The reader's V5 'supports' label is removed because it rests on task accuracy, not on induction-head formation.

versions.untested_parts: No induction heads, previous-token heads, composition, or repeated-token copying are identified or tested.
The paper reports accuracy transitions during training, but does not measure induction-head timing or the claimed simultaneous loss bump and token-index ICL gain.
It does not measure loss falling with token index, the proportion of ICL carried by induction heads, or ICL in large transformers in the sense specified by this version.
No induction behaviour is surveyed across model families, modalities, or architectures.
The study varies data and training setup and reports CoT-ICL accuracy effects, but does not test whether induction heads form or whether their formation depends on those conditions.
It does not isolate few-shot task learning from repeated-token copying or establish which heads or mechanisms carry few-shot learning.
It does not analyze induction-head formation as a sequence of sub-steps or overlapping transitions.

rows.subject: TF-4
rows.size_stated: ≈ 240M parameters without the embedding layer; Table 1 gives 243,288,064
rows.operation_detail: Train on synthetic CoT or non-CoT ICL sequences and evaluate query-answer accuracy during training.
rows.baseline: Non-CoT approach; it does not show the described transition even toward the end of training.
rows.value: CoT accuracy shows a sudden jump after ≈ 8 × 10^5 sequences.
rows.note: The text reports the transition and non-CoT comparison; plotted accuracy values are not stated.
rows.check: CoT-vs-non-CoT accuracy jump on a synthetic task. It is not induction-head formation or ICL persistence, so it does not bear on V5 or V2.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic CoT-ICL task accuracy across vocabulary, number of in-context examples, and pre-training conditions
reader_labels.reason: The reported CoT-ICL accuracy outcomes vary with setup: TF-4 fails in some larger-vocabulary settings at K = 30 but reaches parity with larger models at K = 40, and pre-training advances the transition (r1–r7). This supports setup dependence of ICL performance, not setup dependence of induction-head formation.
